title: QUIC RFC 9000 Server Connection ID Adoption And Continuity Work Item
summary: Close the RFC 9000 Section 7.2 server Source Connection ID adoption and continuity floor for client and server establishment paths.
planned_changes:
- Add focused requirement-home tests for first server Initial adoption, Retry-first adoption, post-Retry first-Initial processing without outbound Destination Connection ID replacement, 0-RTT post-adoption formatting, strict conflicting-source discard after the first valid server Initial, server first-client-Initial Destination Connection ID derivation, and NEW_CONNECTION_ID-only later Destination Connection ID changes.
- Add a shared S7P2 server connection-ID helper for client bootstrap, retry replay, server handshake flight generation, packet receipt, 0-RTT formatting, deferred Handshake buffer inspection, and long-header CID assertions.
- Make the default client establishment path reject later long-header packets with a different server Source Connection ID after the first valid server Initial has been observed.
- Keep the replacement peer Initial reset behavior from REQ-QUIC-CRT-0146 as an explicit internal opt-in for its focused proof and the interop harness multiconnect client case.
- Link the focused proof to dedicated architecture and verification artifacts.
verification_plan: Run the focused S7P2 0009 through 0014 requirement-home filter, run the affected CRT/S5P2P1/S12P2 compatibility filter, run the broader S7P2 requirement-home filter after a Release build, regenerate QUIC requirement coverage triage, validate SpecTrace JSON, and check the diff for whitespace errors.
out_of_scope: Public API changes for the replacement-peer-Initial opt-in.
Complete connection-ID lifecycle parity beyond the Section 7.2 adoption and conflicting-source floor.
completion_notes: Completed as a focused RFC 9000 Section 7.2 server Source Connection ID adoption and continuity proof over the runtime establishment path, internal host settings, interop-harness opt-in boundary, and S7P2 requirement-home tests.
